page: Microsoft Azure M64-32ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It runs on an Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at 2.7 GHz, providing 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 38 MB L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX-512f, AES, and FMA. A defining architectural aspect is the massive allocation of 1792.0 GB of system memory, resulting in 56.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as a 2199 GB solid-state drive (SSD), while no hardware GPU acceleration is included.

Benchmark results reveal clear performance characteristics. Single-core throughput is constrained, as demonstrated by low ratings in single-core stress-ng (1038.39) and Geekbench single-core testing (900.0), as well as bottom-decile compression speeds for single-threaded gzip and bzip3. In contrast, parallel execution scales into the average tier, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 7889.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 102.38 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows read bandwidth of 1218.52 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and 149.32 GB/sec for 256 MB uncached blocks, alongside 82.67 GB/sec write bandwidth. In application tests, Redis SET throughput delivers 20.7 million operations per second, PassMark database operations reach 8453.76, and static web serving achieves 17.08 GB/sec. CPU-based LLM token generation remains weak to poor.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the M64-32ms trades single-threaded compute velocity for exceptional RAM density and substantial local SSD scratch space. This profile is not cost-effective for compute-bound or single-threaded workloads. Instead, it suits memory-heavy enterprise deployments such as in-memory database engines (including SAP HANA or large Redis clusters), large-scale data warehousing, real-time analytics caches, and heavy enterprise transaction processing systems where massive dataset retention in memory is mandatory.
description: Microsoft Azure M64-32ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores. Engineered for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, it features an extensive 1792.0 GB RAM footprint, translating to 56.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 2199 GB of local SSD storage with zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results position its single-core compute performance in the lower tier, whereas multi-core execution, PassMark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth tests fall solidly within average industry tiers. Memory bandwidth reaches 149.32 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 82.67 GB/sec for writes, sustaining 20.7 million Redis SET operations per second. The server trades per-core execution speeds for massive memory capacity, making it a tailored platform for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, and high-footprint enterprise data workloads.
